post.description:
Creates a new table in the specified workspace. The structure of the table - its columns, their data types and any lookup relationships - is defined entirely through the CONFIG parameter at creation time.

The response returns only the view ID of the new table. Use the Get Table Metadata API to inspect the column schema of the table that was created.

simpleTable.summary: Creates a table with basic text, date, currency and number columns in the default folder.

lookupTable.summary: Creates a table inside a named folder whose first column looks up a column of an existing parent table, and hides one column.

mandatoryPiiTable.summary: Creates a table with an auto number key, mandatory columns, PII markers and a default value.

tableCreated.summary: The view ID of the newly created table is returned.

x-zenesis-statuscodes.description: A table or view with the same name already exists in the workspace.
x-zenesis-statuscodes.resolution: Use a TABLENAME that is unique within the workspace.

x-zenesis-statuscodes.description: The specified data type is not compatible with the configuration of the column.
x-zenesis-statuscodes.resolution: Verify the DATATYPE value and the associated format settings.

x-zenesis-statuscodes.resolution: Provide a non-empty COLUMNNAME for every column in the COLUMNS array.

x-zenesis-statuscodes.description: A column name exceeds the maximum allowed length.
x-zenesis-statuscodes.resolution: Keep every COLUMNNAME value within 1000 characters.

x-zenesis-statuscodes.description: Duplicate column names were found in the COLUMNS array.
x-zenesis-statuscodes.resolution: Ensure that every COLUMNNAME value is unique within the table definition.

x-zenesis-statuscodes.description: A DEFAULT value was provided for an AUTO_NUMBER column.
x-zenesis-statuscodes.resolution: Remove the DEFAULT key from AUTO_NUMBER column definitions.

x-zenesis-statuscodes.description: The specified FOLDERNAME does not exist in this workspace.
x-zenesis-statuscodes.resolution: Use the Get Folder List API to verify the exact folder display name before calling this API.

x-zenesis-statuscodes.description: The DATATYPE value is not a recognised data type.
x-zenesis-statuscodes.resolution: Use one of the values listed in the DATATYPE attribute.

x-zenesis-statuscodes.description: The data type of the lookup column is incompatible with the data type of the referenced column.
x-zenesis-statuscodes.resolution: Ensure that both columns use compatible data types.

x-zenesis-statuscodes.description: The user does not have permission to perform this action.
x-zenesis-statuscodes.resolution: Ensure that the user is a Workspace Admin or has Create Table permission on the workspace.

x-zenesis-statuscodes.description: A lookup column cannot refer to a column within the same table.
x-zenesis-statuscodes.resolution: Set LOOKUPCOLUMN.TABLENAME to a different existing table, not the table being created.

x-zenesis-statuscodes.description: The column specified in LOOKUPCOLUMN.COLUMNNAME does not exist in the referenced table.
x-zenesis-statuscodes.resolution: Verify the column name using the Get Table Metadata API on the referenced table.

x-zenesis-statuscodes.description: TABLENAME is missing or null.
x-zenesis-statuscodes.resolution: Ensure that the tableDesign.TABLENAME key is present and non-empty.

x-zenesis-statuscodes.description: The number of columns exceeds the maximum allowed for a table.
x-zenesis-statuscodes.resolution: Reduce the number of entries in the COLUMNS array.

1.value:
Note:
  • The COLUMNS array must hold at least one column. An empty array is rejected.
  • Column names must be unique within the table. Duplicate names fail with error 7128.
  • Columns appear in the table in the order in which they are listed in the COLUMNS array.
  • FOLDERNAME accepts the display name of the folder, not its ID. The name is resolved to an internal folder ID at request time and the request fails with error 7144 when the folder does not exist. Use the Get Folder List API to confirm the name.
  • An AUTO_NUMBER column cannot carry a DEFAULT value. Including one returns error 7143.
  • For a lookup column, the referencing and the referenced columns must have compatible data types, and the referenced table must be a different, existing table in the workspace.
  • When several related tables are created in sequence, create the parent table first and then the child tables that refer to it through LOOKUPCOLUMN.
  • PII is a data-governance marker only. It does not restrict access to the column or encrypt its data.
  • The response returns only viewId. Call the Get Table Metadata API to retrieve the full column schema of the new table.

get.description:
Returns the complete column schema of the specified table, including column names, data types, descriptions, lookup relationships, formula expressions and formatting details.

Only the columns that the calling user has been granted access to are included in the response.

basicColumns.summary: A table with text, date and currency columns, showing the type-specific formatting keys.

lookupColumn.summary: A table whose first column is a lookup, showing pkTableName and pkColumnName populated.

formulaColumn.summary: A table with a formula column, showing the expression in formulaDisplayName.

x-zenesis-statuscodes.description: The specified view does not exist.
x-zenesis-statuscodes.resolution: Verify the view-id using the Get View List API.

x-zenesis-statuscodes.description: The user does not have permission to perform this action.
x-zenesis-statuscodes.resolution: Ensure that the user is a Workspace Admin or has Design Modify permission on the specified view.

x-zenesis-statuscodes.description: The specified view ID does not belong to the given workspace.
x-zenesis-statuscodes.resolution: Confirm that the view-id belongs to the workspace identified by workspace-id.

x-zenesis-statuscodes.description: The specified view is not a table.
x-zenesis-statuscodes.resolution: This API returns metadata only for tables. Use the Get View List API to confirm the view type before calling.

1.value:
Note:
  • The columns array reflects only the subset of columns that the caller has access to. A Workspace Admin or a user with full Design Modify permission sees every column, while a user with restricted view-level sharing sees only the shared columns. A short column list therefore does not necessarily mean that the table has few columns.
  • This API works only on tables. Calling it with the view ID of a report, chart or dashboard returns error 7397. Use the Get View List API to confirm the view type beforehand.
  • pkTableName, pkColumnName, formulaDisplayName, defaultValue and columnDesc are present in every column object and are returned as empty strings when they do not apply. A non-empty pkTableName identifies a lookup column and a non-empty formulaDisplayName identifies a formula column.
  • dateFormat, durationFormat, timeFormat, currencyFormat, thousandSeparator, decimalSeparator and decimalPlaces are returned only for the column types to which they apply and are absent otherwise.
  • columnId is a numeric identifier internally but is serialized as a quoted string.
  • Columns are returned in ascending order of columnIndex, which matches the order shown in the Zoho Analytics interface.

post.description:
Adds one or more columns to an existing table. The API supports two modes in a single endpoint.

- **Single-column mode** - `columnName` and `dataType` are sent at the top level of CONFIG. The ID of the new column is returned.
- **Bulk mode** - a `columns` array holding several column definitions is sent. Every column is added in one request and individual column IDs are not returned.

The mode is selected from the payload: when a `columns` key is present, bulk mode is used regardless of whether `columnName` is also sent.

singleColumn.summary: Adds one plain text column to the table.

singlePiiColumn.summary: Adds one currency column that is marked as holding personally identifiable information.

bulkColumns.summary: Adds several columns of different data types in a single request.

bulkMandatoryColumns.summary: Adds mandatory columns in bulk, each carrying the default value that becomes mandatory alongside isMandatory.

singleModeResult.summary: In single-column mode the ID of the new column is returned in the data key.

bulkModeResult.summary: In bulk mode only the status and the summary are returned, without any column IDs.

x-zenesis-statuscodes.description: A column with the same name already exists in the table.
x-zenesis-statuscodes.resolution: Use a columnName that is unique within the table.

x-zenesis-statuscodes.description: The user does not have permission to perform this action.
x-zenesis-statuscodes.resolution: Ensure that the user is a Workspace Admin or has Design Modify permission on the workspace.

x-zenesis-statuscodes.description: The specified view is not a table.
x-zenesis-statuscodes.resolution: This API operates only on tables. Verify the view type using the Get View List API.

single.name: Single Column Attributes
single.description: Applicable when a single column is added. The ID of the new column is returned in the response.

bulk.name: Bulk Column Attributes
bulk.description: Applicable when several columns are added in one request through the columns array. Individual column IDs are not returned.

1.value:
Note:
  • The mode is detected from the payload. When CONFIG holds a columns key, bulk mode is used and any top-level columnName and dataType keys are ignored. When no columns key is present, single-column mode is used.
  • Single-column mode returns the new columnId. Bulk mode returns only the status and summary - call the Get Table Metadata API afterwards to retrieve the IDs of the newly added columns.
  • In bulk mode, a column entry that sets isMandatory to true must also carry a default value. The request fails when default is absent for such an entry.
  • The maximum number of columns per bulk request is configurable at the organisation level and defaults to 10. Exceeding it returns error 8173.
  • Every columnName must be unique within the table. Adding a column with an existing name returns error 7157.
  • The request is rejected with error 7092 when the table is locked by an in-progress import or schema operation. Retry once the import completes.
  • This API operates only on tables. The view-id must be that of a table, obtained from the Get View List API.

put.description:
Renames the specified column of a table. The column is identified by its column ID in the request URL.

Every view, formula and report that refers to the column is updated automatically to use the new name.

columnRename.summary: Sets a new display name for the column identified in the request URL.

204.description: Column renamed successfully. No response body is returned.

x-zenesis-statuscodes.description: A DDL lock is active on the table.
x-zenesis-statuscodes.resolution: Wait for the in-progress operation to complete and then retry.

x-zenesis-statuscodes.description: The specified column does not exist in the table.
x-zenesis-statuscodes.resolution: Verify the column-id using the Get Table Metadata API.

x-zenesis-statuscodes.description: A column with the new name already exists in the table.
x-zenesis-statuscodes.resolution: Use a column name that is unique within the table.

x-zenesis-statuscodes.description: The column name already exists.
x-zenesis-statuscodes.resolution: Use a columnName that is unique within the table.

x-zenesis-statuscodes.description: The table is a snapshot table and its columns cannot be renamed.
x-zenesis-statuscodes.resolution: Snapshot tables are read-only with respect to their schema. Create a new table when schema changes are needed.

x-zenesis-statuscodes.description: The user does not have permission to perform this action.
x-zenesis-statuscodes.resolution: Ensure that the user is a Workspace Admin or has Design Modify permission on the workspace.

x-zenesis-statuscodes.description: The specified view is not a table.
x-zenesis-statuscodes.resolution: Provide the view ID of a table.

1.value:
Note:
  • This API returns HTTP 204 No Content with no response body on success. There is no status or summary key to parse - treat the HTTP status code as the sole success indicator.
  • The rename propagates automatically. Reports, charts, pivot tables and formula columns that refer to this column are updated to use the new name, so no manual update of the dependent views is needed.
  • Renaming a column to its existing name succeeds without an error.
  • The request is rejected with error 7092 when the table is locked by an in-progress import.
  • Columns of a snapshot table cannot be renamed and return error 7164.
  • An unknown column ID returns error 7107. Verify the column-id using the Get Table Metadata API.
  • Although a rename is safe because every reference is updated, calling the Get Column Dependents API first is good practice before a bulk rename.

delete.description:
Permanently deletes a column from the specified table.

By default the deletion is blocked when any dependent view, report, chart or formula refers to the column. Set `deleteDependentViews` to true to delete those dependents along with the column.

safeDelete.summary: Deletes the column only when no dependent view refers to it. The request is blocked with error 7277 when dependents exist.

cascadeDelete.summary: Deletes the column together with every dependent view, report, chart, pivot table and formula that refers to it.

204.description: Column deleted successfully. No response body is returned.

x-zenesis-statuscodes.description: A DDL lock is active on the table.
x-zenesis-statuscodes.resolution: Wait for the in-progress operation to complete and then retry.

x-zenesis-statuscodes.description: The specified column does not exist in the table.
x-zenesis-statuscodes.resolution: Verify the column-id using the Get Table Metadata API.

x-zenesis-statuscodes.description: The column has dependent views and the deletion has been blocked.
x-zenesis-statuscodes.resolution: Call the Get Column Dependents API to identify them, then either delete them first or set deleteDependentViews to true to delete them along with the column.

x-zenesis-statuscodes.description: The user does not have permission to perform this action.
x-zenesis-statuscodes.resolution: Ensure that the user is a Workspace Admin or has Design Modify permission on the workspace.

x-zenesis-statuscodes.description: The specified view is not a table.
x-zenesis-statuscodes.resolution: Provide the view ID of a table.

1.value:
Note:
  • This API returns HTTP 204 No Content with no response body on success. There is no status or summary key to parse - treat the HTTP status code as the sole success indicator.
  • Call the Get Column Dependents API before deleting. The views, custom formulas and aggregate formulas it lists determine whether a safe deletion or a cascade deletion is appropriate.
  • Setting deleteDependentViews to true is irreversible. Every dependent view, report, chart, pivot table, query table and formula column is permanently deleted along with the column.
  • The request is rejected with error 7092 when the table is locked by an in-progress import.
  • An unknown column ID returns error 7107.

put.description:
Changes the display order of the columns of the specified table. The complete set of non-system column IDs must be sent in the wanted order, because this API does not support reordering a subset of the columns.

This API is not available in white label or client portal contexts and can be called only through the standard host.

reorderAllColumns.summary: Sends the complete ordered set of column IDs of a three-column table, moving the third column to the front.

moveLastToFirst.summary: Moves the last column of a four-column table to the first position, with every other column resent in its existing order.

204.description: Column order updated successfully. No response body is returned.

x-zenesis-statuscodes.description: The user does not have permission to perform this action.
x-zenesis-statuscodes.resolution: Ensure that the user is a Workspace Admin or has Design Modify permission on the view.

x-zenesis-statuscodes.description: The view ID does not belong to the specified workspace.
x-zenesis-statuscodes.resolution: Confirm that the view-id is correct.

x-zenesis-statuscodes.description: One or more non-system columns are missing from the columns array.
x-zenesis-statuscodes.resolution: Include every non-system column ID of the table in the array, not only the ones being moved.

x-zenesis-statuscodes.description: One or more column IDs in the columns array do not belong to this view.
x-zenesis-statuscodes.resolution: Verify every column ID using the Get Table Metadata API.

1.value:
Note:
  • This API returns HTTP 204 No Content with no response body on success. There is no status or summary key to parse - treat the HTTP status code as the sole success indicator.
  • The full column set is required on every call. Unlike the Hide Columns and Show Columns APIs, this one rejects a partial list with error 8179, so a column cannot be moved without also listing every other column in its existing position.
  • System columns, such as the row ID and the audit columns, are excluded from the required set and cannot be reordered.
  • The order of the array defines the display order. The position of each ID becomes the new left-to-right position of that column.
  • Column IDs must be sent as quoted strings, not as integers.
  • A duplicate ID is de-duplicated and only its first occurrence is used, so the array is treated as an ordered set.
  • A column ID that is not present in the table returns error 8180.
  • This API is disabled for white label portal contexts. Calls made through a custom portal domain fail.
  • Obtain the column IDs from the Get Table Metadata API, excluding the system columns, and call it again afterwards to confirm the new column positions.

put.description:
Hides one or more columns of the specified table. Hidden columns are not visible to users viewing the table but are retained in the schema and can be made visible again using the Show Columns API.

At least one column must remain visible at all times.

hideSingleColumn.summary: Hides a single column of the table.

hideMultipleColumns.summary: Hides several columns of the table in one request.

204.description: Columns hidden successfully. No response body is returned.

x-zenesis-statuscodes.description: Hiding these columns would leave no visible column in the table.
x-zenesis-statuscodes.resolution: Ensure that at least one column is left out of the columnIds array.

x-zenesis-statuscodes.description: One or more of the column IDs do not exist in the table.
x-zenesis-statuscodes.resolution: Verify every ID using the Get Table Metadata API.

x-zenesis-statuscodes.description: The user does not have permission to perform this action.
x-zenesis-statuscodes.resolution: Ensure that the user is a Workspace Admin or has Design Modify permission on the view.

x-zenesis-statuscodes.description: The specified view is not a table.
x-zenesis-statuscodes.resolution: This API works only on tables.

1.value:
Note:
  • This API returns HTTP 204 No Content with no response body on success. There is no status or summary key to parse - treat the HTTP status code as the sole success indicator.
  • At least one column must remain visible. When every currently visible column is listed in columnIds, the operation is rejected with error 7089.
  • Column IDs must be sent as quoted strings inside the JSON array, not as integers.
  • Hiding a column that is already hidden is silently ignored. Only the columns that change from visible to hidden are updated.
  • Hidden columns are not deleted. They remain in the schema, continue to take part in formulas and reports, and can be revealed again using the Show Columns API.
  • Obtain the column IDs from the Get Table Metadata API, using the isHidden key to identify the columns that are currently visible.

put.description: Makes one or more previously hidden columns visible again in the specified table.

showSingleColumn.summary: Makes a single hidden column visible again.

showMultipleColumns.summary: Makes several hidden columns visible in one request.

204.description: Columns shown successfully. No response body is returned.

x-zenesis-statuscodes.description: One or more of the column IDs do not exist in the table.
x-zenesis-statuscodes.resolution: Verify every ID using the Get Table Metadata API.

x-zenesis-statuscodes.description: The user does not have permission to perform this action.
x-zenesis-statuscodes.resolution: Ensure that the user is a Workspace Admin or has Design Modify permission on the view.

x-zenesis-statuscodes.description: The specified view is not a table.
x-zenesis-statuscodes.resolution: This API works only on tables.

1.value:
Note:
  • This API returns HTTP 204 No Content with no response body on success. There is no status or summary key to parse - treat the HTTP status code as the sole success indicator.
  • Showing a column that is already visible is silently ignored. Only the columns that change from hidden to visible are updated.
  • Column IDs must be sent as quoted strings inside the JSON array, not as integers.
  • There is no minimum or maximum visible column count for this API. The one-visible-column constraint applies only to the Hide Columns API.
  • Obtain the column IDs from the Get Table Metadata API, using the isHidden key to identify the columns that are currently hidden.

get.description:
Returns every view, custom formula column and aggregate formula that depends on the specified column.

Call this API before deleting or renaming a column to understand the full impact of the change.

withDependents.summary: The column is used by several views and by one custom formula column.

noDependents.summary: Nothing refers to the column, so it can be deleted without any cascade.

x-zenesis-statuscodes.description: The specified column does not exist in the table.
x-zenesis-statuscodes.resolution: Verify the column-id using the Get Table Metadata API.

x-zenesis-statuscodes.description: The user does not have permission to perform this action.
x-zenesis-statuscodes.resolution: Only Workspace Admins can call this API.

x-zenesis-statuscodes.description: The view ID does not belong to the specified workspace.
x-zenesis-statuscodes.resolution: Confirm that the view-id belongs to the workspace identified by workspace-id.

1.value:
Note:
  • Call this API before any destructive column operation. When views or customFormulas are non-empty, setting deleteDependentViews to true in the Delete Column API permanently removes all of those objects.
  • Unlike the other column APIs, which also accept a user with Design Modify permission, this API requires full Workspace Admin access.
  • The views array can list the same view more than once when the column is used in several ways within that view, for example as both a filter and a display column of a query table.
  • Obtain the view-id from the Get View List API and the column-id from the Get Table Metadata API.

put.description:
Sets the default sort order for the rows of the specified table. The API supports two modes.

- **Set sort** - a `columns` array of column IDs and a `sortOrder` are sent to sort the rows by those columns.
- **Reset sort** - `resetSort` is set to true to clear every sort setting on the table.

This API is not available in white label or client portal contexts and can be called only through the standard host.

singleColumnAscending.summary: Sorts the rows of the table by a single column in ascending order.

multiColumnDescending.summary: Sorts the rows by two columns in descending order. The first column ID is the primary sort key.

resetSort.summary: Clears every sort setting that is currently applied to the table.

204.description: Sort order applied successfully. No response body is returned.

x-zenesis-statuscodes.description: The user does not have permission to perform this action.
x-zenesis-statuscodes.resolution: Ensure that the user is a Workspace Admin or has Design Modify permission on the view.

x-zenesis-statuscodes.description: The view ID does not belong to the specified workspace.
x-zenesis-statuscodes.resolution: Confirm that the view-id is correct.

x-zenesis-statuscodes.description: Invalid value for sortOrder.
x-zenesis-statuscodes.resolution: Send 1 for ascending or 2 for descending. No other value is accepted.

x-zenesis-statuscodes.description: One or more column IDs in the columns array do not belong to this view.
x-zenesis-statuscodes.resolution: Verify every column ID using the Get Table Metadata API.

x-zenesis-statuscodes.description: resetSort and sortOrder cannot be used together.
x-zenesis-statuscodes.resolution: Send either resetSort set to true on its own, or columns together with sortOrder without resetSort.

1.value:
Note:
  • This API returns HTTP 204 No Content with no response body on success. There is no status or summary key to parse - treat the HTTP status code as the sole success indicator.
  • This API is disabled for white label portal contexts. Calls made through a custom portal domain fail.
  • The sortOrder value applies uniformly to every column in the columns array. Sorting different columns in different directions is not supported through this API - use a report or a query table configuration instead.
  • The order of the columns array defines the sort priority. The first column ID is the primary sort key and the remaining IDs are the secondary and tertiary keys.
  • Column IDs must be sent as quoted strings, not as integers.
  • Sending resetSort together with sortOrder or columns returns error 8182 and no change is made. After a reset, every column reports sortedOrder as 0 and sortedIndex as -1.
  • A column ID that is not present in the table returns error 8180.
  • Use the Get Table Metadata API afterwards to confirm the sortedOrder and sortedIndex values of the affected columns.

post.description:
Creates a lookup relationship from the specified child column to a column in a reference table. A lookup links two tables of a workspace through a shared column, in the same way that a foreign key constraint links two relational tables.

The child column identified by `column-id` in the request URL is the many side of the relationship, and `referenceColumnId` in the reference table is the one, or unique key, side. Once the relationship exists, multi-table reports, pivot tables and query tables can pull data from both tables without a manual join, and the relationship becomes visible in the Schema View of the workspace.

customerLookup.summary: Links the Customer ID column of the Order Details table to the unique Customer ID column of the Customers table.

productLookup.summary: Links the Product Code column of the Sales table to the unique Product Code column of the Products table.

204.description: Lookup added successfully. No response body is returned.

x-zenesis-statuscodes.description: The specified child column does not exist in the child table.
x-zenesis-statuscodes.resolution: Verify the column-id using the Get Table Metadata API on the child view.

x-zenesis-statuscodes.description: The child column is itself a lookup-derived column, and a lookup on a lookup is not allowed.
x-zenesis-statuscodes.resolution: Use a regular base column of the child table, not a column pulled in from a parent table through an existing lookup.

x-zenesis-statuscodes.description: The child column and the reference column have incompatible data types.
x-zenesis-statuscodes.resolution: Ensure that both columns share a compatible data type. For GEO columns the geo role level must match as well.

x-zenesis-statuscodes.description: Adding this lookup would create a circular relationship chain across tables.
x-zenesis-statuscodes.resolution: Review the existing relationships and choose a reference table that does not already refer to the child table, either directly or transitively.

x-zenesis-statuscodes.description: A lookup relationship already exists on this child column.
x-zenesis-statuscodes.resolution: Remove the existing lookup using the Remove Lookup API and then add the new one.

x-zenesis-statuscodes.description: The user does not have permission to perform this action.
x-zenesis-statuscodes.resolution: Ensure that the user is a Workspace Admin or has Design Modify permission on the workspace.

x-zenesis-statuscodes.description: The reference table does not belong to the same workspace as the child table.
x-zenesis-statuscodes.resolution: Both tables must belong to the workspace identified by workspace-id.

x-zenesis-statuscodes.description: An identical lookup relationship between the same child column and the same reference column is already defined.
x-zenesis-statuscodes.resolution: No action is needed because the relationship already exists.

x-zenesis-statuscodes.description: The reference table is the same as the child table, and a self-referential lookup is not allowed.
x-zenesis-statuscodes.resolution: Provide a referenceViewId that is different from the view-id in the request URL.

x-zenesis-statuscodes.description: The reference column holds duplicate values and cannot serve as the reference side.
x-zenesis-statuscodes.resolution: Choose a column in the reference table that holds unique values, or de-duplicate the data of the reference column first.

1.value:
Note:
  • This API returns HTTP 204 No Content with no response body on success. There is no status or summary key to parse - treat the HTTP status code as the sole success indicator.
  • Lookups can be created only between tables. A report, chart, pivot table, query table or dashboard cannot be used as the child view or as the reference view, and both tables must belong to the same workspace.
  • A child column can take part in exactly one lookup relationship. To point the lookup at a different target, call the Remove Lookup API on the column first and then add the new relationship.
  • The uniqueness of the reference column is validated before the relationship is created, and duplicate values return error 7509. Uniqueness is checked only at creation time - it is not enforced for rows inserted into the reference table afterwards.
  • For GEO and GEO_NUM columns, the geo role level must match between the child and the reference column, such as country to country or city to city. A mismatch returns error 7183.
  • An AUTO_NUMBER column cannot be used as the reference column.
  • referenceViewId and referenceColumnId are sent as unquoted numbers, unlike the column ID arrays of the Hide Columns and Show Columns APIs, which are sent as strings.
  • Adding a lookup has no effect on existing reports. It is the removal of a lookup that can break reports spanning the two tables.
  • Resolve the IDs in this order: Get View List for the child view-id and for referenceViewId, then Get Table Metadata on each table for column-id and referenceColumnId.

1.value:
Note:
  • This API returns HTTP 204 No Content with no response body on success. There is no status or summary key to parse - treat the HTTP status code as the sole success indicator.
  • This API is not idempotent. A variable ID that does not exist, or that was already deleted, returns an error rather than a silent success.
  • The deletion is blocked whenever the variable is used in a formula, a report filter or a SQL query of the workspace, so that those dependents are not broken.
  • There is no cascade option here, unlike the Delete Column and Delete Aggregate Formula APIs. The dependent references must always be removed manually first.
  • There is no dedicated dependents API for variables. Review the formula expressions, through the Get Custom Formulas and Get Aggregate Formula APIs, along with the report and query definitions, looking for ${variableName} references before deleting.

Returns the full definition of a specific variable, including its values or range, every per-user override and its display format.

Call this API before the Edit Variable API, which replaces the whole definition and therefore needs the current state to be fetched first.

listVariable.summary: A List-type variable with two per-user overrides and a workspace-wide fallback.

rangeVariable.summary: A Range-type numeric variable with no per-user override, showing the numeric formatting keys.

allValuesVariable.summary: An All Values-type variable, whose response carries no defaultData key at all.

1.value:
Note:
  • variableType and variableDataType are returned as native integers by this API but as quoted strings by the Get Variables API. Take care when comparing or switching on these attributes across the two read APIs.
  • defaultData may be absent entirely. An All Values variable carries no such key, so check for its presence before reading its sub-attributes.
  • The contents of format depend on variableDataType. Read currencySymbol and showNegativeSign only for a Currency variable and showPercent only for a Percentage variable, because those keys are omitted for the other data types.
  • The entries of values, along with minValue, maxValue, stepSize and defaultValue, are always strings even for the numeric data types, so that precision is preserved. Parse them into numbers when further calculation is needed.
  • Branch the parsing on variableType first and then on variableDataType, because the shape of defaultData, of the userSpecificData entries and of format all depend on those two attributes.
  • Obtain the variable-id from the Get Variables API.

DefaultVariableData.title: DefaultVariableData
DefaultVariableData.description: JSONObject that holds the workspace-wide fallback definition, applied to any user who is not covered by a `userSpecificData` entry. It is mandatory for a List or a Range variable and is ignored for an All Values variable. The fields that apply depend on `variableType`: `values` and `defaultValue` for List, and `minValue`, `maxValue`, `stepSize` and `defaultValue` for Range.

minValue.description: Lower bound of the range, for a Range variable. Sent as a string even for numeric data types, so that precision is preserved.

maxValue.description: Upper bound of the range, for a Range variable. Must be greater than `minValue`.

stepSize.description: Increment between the selectable values of a Range variable. It must be non-zero, must not exceed the span of the range, and must divide that span evenly.

defaultValue.description: Value used when the variable is resolved without further input. For a List variable it must be one of the entries of `values`, and for a Range variable it must fall between `minValue` and `maxValue`.

expression.description: New aggregate expression, which fully replaces the existing one.

description.description: New description for the aggregate formula.
examples: Total net sales after returns and discounts

columnPriority.description: Ranking priority of this formula when several metrics could match a natural-language query.

EditFormulaColumnConfig.title: EditFormulaColumnConfig
EditFormulaColumnConfig.description: Configuration that holds the new expression of the formula column, together with any attribute to be updated alongside it.

expression.description: New formula expression, which fully replaces the existing one. The complete expression must be resent even for a minor change.

formulaName.description: New display name for the formula column. It is sent as part of the configuration rather than as a separate argument, because the SDK method takes only the formula ID and the expression positionally.

description.description: New description for the formula column. Resend this explicitly whenever its value matters, because the behaviour of unset optional text fields is not guaranteed to preserve the existing value.

examples: SELECT Region, SUM(SalesAmount) AS TotalSales FROM Sales WHERE Year = 2026 GROUP BY Region

sortedOrder.description: Sort direction currently applied to the column.

sortedIndex.description: Priority of this column when several columns take part in the sort order. Returned as -1 when the column is not part of any sort order.

dateFormat.description: Date or date-time format string. Returned only for `DATE` and `DATE_AS_DATE` columns.

durationFormat.description: Duration format string. Returned only for `DURATION` columns.

timeFormat.description: Time format string. Returned only for `TIME` columns.

currencyFormat.description: Currency locale format string. Returned only for `CURRENCY` columns.

thousandSeparator.description: Thousands separator character. Returned for the numeric column types `CURRENCY`, `NUMBER`, `DECIMAL_NUMBER` and `PERCENT`.

decimalSeparator.description: Decimal separator character. Returned for numeric column types.

decimalPlaces.description: Number of decimal places configured for the column. Returned for numeric column types.

TableColumnMetadataList.title: TableColumnMetadataList
TableColumnMetadataList.description: JSONArray of column definitions, ordered by ascending column index. Only the columns that the calling user has access to are returned.

TableDesign.title: TableDesign
TableDesign.description: JSONObject that holds the complete design definition of the new table.

TABLENAME.description: Display name for the new table. Must be unique within the workspace.

FOLDERNAME.description: Display name of an existing folder in which the table has to be placed. When omitted, the table is placed in the workspace's default folder.

TableMetadata.title: TableMetadata
TableMetadata.description: JSONObject that holds the metadata of the table.

UserSpecificVariableData.title: UserSpecificVariableData
UserSpecificVariableData.description: JSONObject that overrides the values, range and default of the variable for a specific set of users. The value fields follow the same rules as `defaultData`, and `defaultValue` is optional here.

minValue.description: Lower bound of the range for these users, for a Range variable.

maxValue.description: Upper bound of the range for these users, for a Range variable.

stepSize.description: Increment between the selectable values for these users, for a Range variable.

defaultValue.description: Default value applied for these users. It does not apply to an All Values variable.

domainName.description: Portal domain whose user base this entry applies to. It is relevant only for a White Label or Client Portal workspace that serves several custom domains, and should be omitted for a standard workspace.

UserSpecificVariableDataList.title: UserSpecificVariableDataList
UserSpecificVariableDataList.description: JSONArray of per-user override entries. Any user whose email address is not listed in one of these entries resolves the variable through `defaultData`.

VariableConfig.title: VariableConfig
VariableConfig.description: Configuration that holds the complete definition of a workspace variable. The Edit Variable API uses the same structure and requires the full definition to be resent, because it replaces rather than patches the variable.

variableName.description: Display name of the variable. Must be unique within the workspace, and the check is case-insensitive. The name cannot start with `system.` or `${`, and cannot end with `}`, because those patterns are reserved for system variables.

variableDataType.description: Data type that the values of the variable must conform to. A Range variable requires one of the numeric data types, because Range is not supported for text.

variableType.description:
Determines how the variable resolves a value.

- **0** - List. The value is chosen from a fixed set of allowed values, with one default value.
- **1** - Range. The value is chosen from a numeric range defined by a minimum, a maximum and a step size, with one default value.
- **3** - All Values. The variable represents every possible value and no list, range or default is defined.

The reserved internal type 2 is not accepted through this API.

VariableDetails.title: VariableDetails
VariableDetails.description: JSONObject that holds the full definition of the variable, including its values or range, every per-user override and its display format.

variableType.description: How the variable resolves a value. It is returned as a native integer by this API, whereas the Get Variables API returns the same information as a quoted string.

variableDataType.description: Data type of the values of the variable. It is returned as a native integer by this API, whereas the Get Variables API returns it as a quoted string.

VariableEmailIds.title: VariableEmailIds
VariableEmailIds.description: JSONArray of the email addresses of the users that this override applies to. It cannot be empty, and an address may appear in only one override entry per variable.

VariableFormat.title: VariableFormat
VariableFormat.description: JSONObject that holds the display formatting of the value of the variable. The keys that apply depend on `variableDataType` - the currency keys apply only to a Currency variable and `showPercent` only to a Percentage variable.

alignment.description: Alignment used when the value is displayed.

decimalPlaces.description: Number of decimal places to display, for the numeric data types. Send -1 for automatic precision.

userLocale.description: Controls whether the number is formatted according to the locale settings of the viewing user rather than a fixed format.

thousandSeparator.description: Selector for the thousands grouping symbol, for the numeric data types. The codes depend on the locale of the workspace, and 0 is the default.

decimalSeparator.description: Selector for the decimal point symbol, for the numeric data types. The codes depend on the locale of the workspace, and 0 is the default full stop.

units.description: Custom unit label appended to the value, for the numeric data types. Returned as None when no unit is set.

numberingType.description: Selector for the numbering system used when the value is displayed, such as the standard or the Indian numbering system.

currencySymbol.description: Locale-formatted currency symbol, for a Currency variable.

showNegativeSign.description: Controls whether a negative currency value is shown with a minus sign rather than in parentheses, for a Currency variable.

showPercent.description: Controls whether the percent symbol is appended to the displayed value, for a Percentage variable.

dateFormat.description: Reserved key inherited from the shared formatting template. It has no effect on a variable, because no date data type is supported.

VariableList.title: VariableList
VariableList.description: JSONArray of the variables defined in the workspace. Returned as an empty array when there are none. The values, the range and the format of a variable are not included here - use the Get Variable Details API for the full definition.

VariableListData.title: VariableListData
VariableListData.description: JSONObject that holds the list of variables.

VariableSummary.title: VariableSummary
VariableSummary.description: JSONObject that holds the summary details of a variable.

variableId.description: Unique ID of the variable. Send this value as variable-id in the Edit Variable, Delete Variable and Get Variable Details APIs.

variableType.description: How the variable resolves a value. It is returned as a quoted string by this API, whereas the Get Variable Details API returns the same information as a native integer.

variableDataType.description: Data type of the values of the variable. It is returned as a quoted string by this API, whereas the Get Variable Details API returns it as a native integer.

VariableValues.title: VariableValues
VariableValues.description: JSONArray of the allowed values, for a List variable. The entries are sent as strings even for numeric data types, so that precision is preserved.

items.description: An allowed value of the variable.

ViewAggregateFormula.title: ViewAggregateFormula
ViewAggregateFormula.description: JSONObject that holds the details of an aggregate formula owned by the view.

formulaId.description: Unique ID of the aggregate formula. Send this value as formula-id in the view-scoped Edit and Delete APIs and in the workspace-scoped Get Dependents and Get Value APIs.

formulaName.description: Display name of the aggregate formula.

expression.description: Aggregate expression of the formula. Returned as an empty string when the calling user does not have edit permission on this formula.

description.description: Description of the aggregate formula. Empty when no description is set.

subtypeId.description: Internal numeric code for the result data type of the formula. It is inferred from the aggregate function and the source columns and cannot be set explicitly.

subtypeName.description: Display-form internal code for the result data type. The workspace-scoped Get Unified Metrics in Workspace API returns the same information under the key `subtype` instead.

ViewAggregateFormulaData.title: ViewAggregateFormulaData
ViewAggregateFormulaData.description: JSONObject that holds the list of aggregate formulas owned by the view.

ViewAggregateFormulaList.title: ViewAggregateFormulaList
ViewAggregateFormulaList.description: JSONArray of the aggregate formulas owned by this view. Returned as an empty array when there are none.

WorkspaceAggregateFormula.title: WorkspaceAggregateFormula
WorkspaceAggregateFormula.description: JSONObject that holds the details of an aggregate formula together with its owning view.

formulaId.description: Unique ID of the aggregate formula. Send this value as formula-id in the Get Aggregate Formula Dependents and Get Aggregate Formula Value APIs.

formulaName.description: Display name of the aggregate formula.

expression.description: Aggregate expression of the formula. Returned as an empty string when the calling user does not have edit permission on this particular formula.

description.description: Description of the aggregate formula. Empty when no description is set.

subtypeId.description: Internal numeric code for the result data type of the formula.

subtype.description: Display-form internal code for the result data type. The view-scoped Get Aggregate Formula API returns the same information under the key `subtypeName` instead.

tableId.description: ID of the table or view that owns this aggregate formula. This can be a query table as well as a regular table.

tableName.description: Display name of the owning table or view.

createdBy.description: Email address of the user who created the formula.

modifiedTime.description: Time of the last modification to the formula, in epoch milliseconds.

WorkspaceAggregateFormulaData.title: WorkspaceAggregateFormulaData
WorkspaceAggregateFormulaData.description: JSONObject that holds the workspace-wide catalogue of aggregate formulas.

WorkspaceAggregateFormulaList.title: WorkspaceAggregateFormulaList
WorkspaceAggregateFormulaList.description: JSONArray of every aggregate formula in the workspace, together with the table or view that owns each one.
